title: Properties Pass Down
short: Every property of rectangles is also true for squares.
trouble: Children say a square cannot be a rectangle, or that a rectangle must have two long and two short sides.

blocks.html: You have seen the family tree of shapes. The tree is useful because properties pass down it: whatever is true of every shape in a family is true of every shape in its smaller families too.
If every rectangle has a property, then every square has it, because every square is a rectangle. Properties pass down the tree, never up: a square's 4 equal sides do not pass up to all rectangles.

“Every rectangle has 4 right angles” is a statement about all rectangles, and squares are among them. So a square must have 4 right angles. It also inherits from parallelograms: opposite sides parallel and equal, opposite angles equal. A square gets its equal sides from the rhombus family.

blocks.name: g5-shapetree
blocks.cap: A rectangle inherits from parallelograms, trapezoids and quadrilaterals. Tap the square to see what it inherits from both rectangles and rhombuses.

blocks.title: What a square inherits
blocks.q: Squares are rectangles. What must every square have because of that?
steps: So every square has 4 right angles. (Its 4 equal sides come from being a rhombus.)

blocks.title: Is a square a rectangle?
blocks.q: Is every square a rectangle? Is every rectangle a square?
steps: A rectangle only needs 4 right angles. Every square has them, so every square is a rectangle.
A square also needs 4 equal sides. Many rectangles do not have them.

blocks.html: Saying a square cannot be a rectangle, or that a rectangle must have two long and two short sides. The rule for a rectangle says nothing about side lengths. Check against the rule itself, not against the picture you usually see.

blocks.name: shapes
blocks.cap: Drag a corner of the square. While the angles stay right angles, it is still a rectangle, even with unequal sides.
